subject.title: feat(cron): configurable minimum interval guardrail for recurring jobs

question: Should `cron.minInterval` become an OpenClaw core config surface and enforceable fail-closed guardrail for recurring cron jobs?
rationale: The implementation is opt-in, but it adds a new operator setting and changes create/update/fire behavior when enabled; that is a product and compatibility-sensitive policy choice rather than a purely mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Approve opt-in core guardrail after docs proof
options.body: Accept `cron.minInterval` as a core cron operator setting once the docs map is regenerated and relevant checks are green.

options.title: Narrow to warning-only behavior
options.body: Reject fail-closed enforcement for now and keep only warning or advisory behavior like the related high-frequency cron warning attempt.

options.title: Defer outside core
options.body: Close or pause this PR until a plugin/ClawHub or broader scheduling policy path is chosen for high-frequency cron control.

recommendation.title: Approve opt-in core guardrail after docs proof
recommendation.body: Accept `cron.minInterval` as a core cron operator setting once the docs map is regenerated and relevant checks are green.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is the requested reviewer and has recent adjacent cron runtime history, making them the best available owner for the config-surface decision.
